_sources.discrepancies: Illinois has no voter ID requirement — voters affirm identity by signing the poll book. NCSL confirms 'no document required'. Voter registration deadline is 28 days before election by mail/online; same-day registration available during early voting and on Election Day. 2026-06-10: Primary confirmed as March 17, 2026 and general as November 3, 2026 (VOTE411). Early-voting start dates corrected to the statutory 40th day before each election (10 ILCS 5/19A-15); the file previously listed later start dates inconsistent with its own 40-day note.

earlyVoting.notes: Early voting began at election authority offices 40 days before the primary (February 5, 2026) and ran through March 16; additional permanent sites open from the 15th day before. Hours and locations vary by election authority.

Early voting begins at election authority main offices 40 days before the election (September 24, 2026) and runs through November 2; additional permanent early voting sites open from the 15th day before (October 19). Hours and locations vary — check your county clerk or board of elections.

Early voting begins at election authority main offices 40 days before the general election (September 24, 2026); permanent early voting sites and hours are set by county clerks and boards of election.

votingRules.phonesAtPollsDetail: Illinois does not prohibit phones at polling places. Voters may not photograph their ballot or other voters. No electioneering within 100 feet of the polling place entrance.
additionalRules: No photo ID required — voters sign the poll book to verify identity.
Open primary: voters request whichever party's ballot they want without declaring affiliation.
Grace period registration available at the county clerk's office up to and including Election Day.
No runoffs in Illinois — the candidate with the most votes wins.

eligibility: Any registered voter may request a vote by mail ballot without providing a reason
voteByMail.applicationDeadline: 5 days before the election (received by county clerk)
voteByMail.returnDeadline: Must be postmarked by Election Day and received within 14 days after, or received by the county clerk by 7 p.m. on Election Day
voteByMail.returnDeadlinePlain: Must be postmarked by Election Day and received within 14 days, or returned in person by poll closing on Election Day.

primaryParticipation.ruleExplanationEn: Illinois has an open primary (10 ILCS 5/7-43). Voters declare their party choice at the polls on primary day and may change their declared affiliation. No advance party registration is required.
primaryParticipation.ruleExplanationEs: Illinois tiene una primaria abierta (10 ILCS 5/7-43). Los votantes declaran su elección de partido en el lugar de votación el día de la primaria y pueden cambiar su afiliación declarada. No se requiere registro de partido previo.
